operator_io_quirks: Tiny DB (Movie 8, Reviewer 8, Rating 14 rows) — no rowid sampling needed; original_values fully read.
Rating has NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must no-op on empty PK tuple, not dedupe all rows.

ratingDate declared 'date' but storage is TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD' (9 distinct, 1 NULL); ts_fuzzer dispatches to Date|Number(int elements) — first element parses as int? '2011-01-22' does NOT parse as int, so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d.
Movie.year declared INT, values 1939..1997 — Number fuzzer, not Year (type is 'int' not 'year').
Movie.director has 1 NULL (null_rate 0.125) though notnull=0; NULLs flow into String sampler and are dropped by Base.
Rating.rID/mID are FK children of Reviewer.rID/Movie.mID; both parents exist and are unique PKs — clean FK fill.
Rating.mID distinct=6 < Movie.mID distinct=8: some movies unreviewed; FK draw with replacement will still cover all parents.
All identifiers are simple mixed-case (Movie, Reviewer, Rating, mID, rID, ratingDate) — no spaces, no quoting hazards beyond case.
No composite keys, no self-references, no dangling FKs, no CHECK/UNIQUE constraints in DDL.
Rating.stars INT 2..5 (4 distinct) — Number fuzzer will produce values far outside [2,5] (range ±10^scale).
ratingDate NULL rate 0.143 (2 of 14) — Date sampler elements include None, dropped by Base; template still from non-null strings.
No views/triggers/indexes in DDL — empty clone is just 3 CREATE TABLEs.
operator_ts_expectations: Movie.mID / Reviewer.rID: Number fuzzer, scale from 'int' (no args) -> range ±10^0? actually int -> scale 0, range [-1,1] perturbed; PK dedupe keeps first occurrence, so ~1-2 distinct PKs survive -> tiny tables.

Movie.title / director, Reviewer.name: String fuzzer, length range from min/max of 5 sampled originals (e.g. 'E.T.' len 4 .. 'Gone with the Wind' len 18), CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() with 50% contaminate — implausible names drive FN on name-equality queries.
Movie.year: Number fuzzer, elements 1939..1997 -> list range [min(el), 10^scale] quirk; fresh draws uniform in [-1,1] mostly -> years like 0, -1, 1 -> FN on year predicates (e.g. year>1990).
Rating.stars: Number fuzzer, elements 2..5 -> list range [2, 10^0=1]? scale 0 -> max=1 < min=2, degenerate; fresh draws in [-1,1] -> stars 0/-1/1 -> FN on stars>=3.

ratingDate: Date fuzzer, template %Y-%m-%d from '2011-01-22'; range [2011-01-12, 2011-01-30] (only 9 distinct, <2 distinct? no, 9) -> fresh dates uniform in that 18-day window -> FN on date-range queries spanning months/years.
Rating has no PK: sample_fresh_primary_keys no-op; drop_unique_duplicates no-op (no unique cols) -> Rating keeps full n rows, FK values drawn from filtered parents.

FK fill: Rating.rID/mID drawn with replacement from Reviewer.rID/Movie.mID final values; if parent PK dedupe collapsed to 1-2 rows, Rating FK values collapse too -> joins return few rows -> FP on COUNT/EXISTS queries.
p=0.2 default, 30% chance whole-instance p=0 -> sometimes all-fresh (implausible) values, sometimes all-original-like.
max_l0 cap (rng*30) on fresh draws -> after ~30 fresh values, reuse -> duplicates in non-PK columns -> FP on DISTINCT/COUNT(DISTINCT) queries.
String contaminate (50%) adds/removes chars -> 'Star Wars' -> 'xStar Wars' etc -> FN on exact title matches.
Date leading-zero strip: '2011-01-22' starts with '2' not '0', contains '-0'? no ('-01' has '-0') -> strip leading zeros -> '2011-1-22' format mismatch -> FN on date string comparisons.
